newsitem.title: UK: UK gives more spectrum to mobile telephone firms.
newsitem.headline: UK gives more spectrum to mobile telephone firms.

text.p: Britain on Wednesday confirmed that the country's two smallest and purely digital cellular telephone companies would be allocated additional spectrum so they could provide new services.

After consultation with the Department of Trade and Industry and the two companies, the Radiocommunications Agency (RA) said it had agreed to give an additional two by five megahertz radio bandwidths to Orange Plc and One2One.

"The additional allocation brings the total allocation for each operator to two by 30 MHz, and completes the process of spectrum allocation to the PCN (personal communications network) operators as indicated in the consultative document," it stated.
The extra bandwidth can be set aside by the two mobile phone companies for use when they experience bandwidth problems.
The decision follows a policy outlined by the DTI and RA in a consultative document published in 1996, called "Mobile phone spectrum over the next decade".

The offer is being mirrored by a similar 1800 megahertz (MHz) offering to the two analogue and digital 900 MHz operators in the UK -- Cellnet and Vodafone Group Plc -- which are developing dual band handsets which work on both frequencies.
The Radiocommunications Agency, an executive arm of the DTI, manages most non-military spectrum in the UK and has income of 43 million stg from charges.
